title: A strict internal form margin gives saturation without opening a photon gap
statement: Assume the source zero-energy Schur form C>=c*I,c>0, positive auxiliary frequencies, M_omega>0 almost everywhere and finite integral V*V^dagger/omega. Then the full signal one-body form and its hard-core-emitter compressed second quantization are nonnegative. For m memory sites Hmem=-B*K+T with T>=0,[T,K]=0 and Dicke-null states in every charge sector, total-N bottom is-B*min(N,m). For N>m it is a soft-photon dissociation threshold, not an extra bound eigenstate. This strict internal margin does not give a global spectral gap.

body: Complete the auxiliary/continuum quadratic forms, using the finite infrared weighted coupling integral, to leave C on the emitter amplitudes. Nonnegative second quantization and compression preserve the form bound. C strictly positive plus positive oscillator/continuum energies rules out a nonvacuum zero-energy signal eigenvector. K<=min(N,m) gives the lower bound. For N<=m use a Dicke-null memory state and signal vacuum; for N>m fill memory and add photons supported arbitrarily near zero energy. Their expectation approaches-B*m without a normalizable zero-energy photon. Positive graph-Laplacian terms J_ij(|10>-|01>)(<10|-<01|) annihilate each equal-amplitude Dicke state. Collective emitter shift chi*(m-K)*I commutes with this interaction, so stationary scattering is identity within each charge space relative to free memory evolution. Heterogeneous site-conditioned shifts generally fail this commutation and cannot silently inherit it.
